findings.title: keychain_has's per-directory cache is never pruned for directories that stop being queried
findings.detail: SEEN is a process-lifetime static Vec keyed by config_dir. An entry is only removed/refreshed when the same config_dir is looked up again (via the retain() call before push). If an account is deleted or its config_dir otherwise stops being queried while it still has a cached 'found' entry, that entry stays in the Vec forever (it's never evicted on expiry, only overwritten on a fresh lookup for that same dir). On a long-running obid process that churns through many accounts over time this grows unboundedly instead of being bounded by the number of currently-configured accounts.

findings.title: keychain_has's cache bypasses the keychain_on() toggle, unlike cursor_keychain_has
findings.detail: cursor_keychain_has() re-checks cursor_keychain_on() on every call before consulting its cache (line 11437), so turning the Cursor Keychain copy off takes effect immediately. keychain_has(), by contrast, returns the cached 'found' result (line 11298-11300) without checking keychain_on() at all; the on/off check only happens inside keychain() on a cache miss. If the Claude Keychain copy is turned off while a recent positive result is cached, has_login/signed_in can keep reporting a login as present for up to LOOK_EVERY (2s) after it should have stopped being considered, diverging from the parallel Cursor implementation added in the same change.
